messages:
Aisha (CSM): Quick sync on Acadia private VPC onboarding — Lina flagged intermittent CloudTrail delivery failures to their SIEM after NAT scaling. Need owners: egress pattern, KMS policy, and any IAM role gaps. @Jon @Samir @Maya can you triage?

Jon (Infra): On it. I pulled NAT GW metrics for the time window — saw port exhaustion spikes around 2026-03-20T15:10Z. Are they using ephemeral port reuse on the proxy? Also: how many concurrent Splunk streams?

Lina (Customer): We run two private subnets (us-west-2a/b) and one NAT GW per AZ. Splunk HEC has 10 concurrent forwarders, TLS to https://ingest.acadia-splunk.corp:8088. We rotated certs last week. Failures started after heavy test traffic.

Samir (Security): Two quick checks: 1) KMS key policy — the key Acadia provided doesn't include Redwood's service principal so our streaming process may be denied on rekey attempts. 2) CloudTrail delivery role must have s3:PutObjectAcl on the destination bucket. If either is off, retries look like "delivery failed" in the Splunk sidecar.

Maya (SRE): Also confirm route table has proper 0.0.0.0/0 -> NAT for private subnets and that there are no conflicting egress NACL rules. I can run a connectivity test from their eni if Lina gives me an instance id.

Lina (Customer): instance id i-0b7c2... — feel free to SSH, or run whatever checks. Ops team said they don't have VPC endpoints; everything goes via NAT.

Jon (Infra): I'll reprogress NAT port exhaustion locally with a load generator. Meanwhile, Lina can you set temporary rate limiting on forwarders if possible? That should reduce bursts.

Samir (Security): KMS snippet suggestion for their key policy (replace ARNs):
```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Sid": "AllowRootUse",
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:root"},
      "Action": "kms:*",
      "Resource": "*"
    },
    {
      "Sid": "AllowRedwoodService",
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::REDACTED:role/redwood-inference-service"},
      "Action": ["kms:Encrypt","kms:Decrypt","kms:GenerateDataKey"],
      "Resource": "*"
    },
    {
      "Sid": "AllowCustomerAudit",
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/acadia-audit-role"},
      "Action": ["kms:DescribeKey","kms:GetPublicKey","kms:ListKeys"],
      "Resource": "*"
    }
  ]
}
```

Aisha (CSM): Thanks Samir — Lina, would you be comfortable adding the Redwood service role to the key policy? We can do it jointly during an access window. Also want to capture renewal risk: if certs or keys rotate without automated rollout, ingestion will break — that raises a 30% renewal risk flag on our side until we get auto-rotation + test harness.

Lina (Customer): Yes, we can add that. Would like a short runbook for one-click rollback if something breaks.

Devex (Solutions): I'll draft a minimal rollback playbook and a quick smoke test script (curl + status check) — will post to the onboarding docs and ping here. Example check: `curl -kS https://ingest.acadia-splunk.corp:8088/services/collector/health` should return HTTP 200.

Maya (SRE): For observability, toggle verbose CloudTrail for 1 hour during the change window and stream logs to a temp bucket prefixed `acadia-debug-`. Make sure lifecycle is short (7d) to limit costs.

ops-bot: New runbook uploaded: https://redwood-internal/runbooks/acadia-kms-egress-rollout — added smoke test + rollback steps.

Jon (Infra): Plan: 1) temporary rate limit on forwarders (Lina) 2) add Redwood role to KMS key policy (Lina + Samir) 3) increase NAT GW port capacity / split flows (Jon) 4) run smoke test (Devex/Maya). Can we schedule a 30-min window tomorrow 09:00 PST?

Lina (Customer): 09:00 PST works. Please include our infra oncall (sylvia@acadia).

Aisha (CSM): Great — I'll send calendar invite and update health score post-cutover. Current renewal risk note: medium until smoke test passes + KMS policy stable. Will change to low after 48h of stable telemetry. :thumbsup:

Samir (Security): One more note: rotate the key material on a weekend if possible. If they insist on weekday, enable automatic backup of key ACLs before rotation.

Maya (SRE): I'll prepare a quick connectivity checklist and paste into the runbook before the window.

Aisha (CSM): Thanks all — marking action items and will follow up in the invite.
